items.title: The Old Game Is Over: Rise of GEO and End of Traditional SEO
items.summary: A detailed post explains how traditional SEO is dying due to AI Overviews, ChatGPT Search, and Perplexity, leading to impressions up but clicks down. It introduces Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) as the new standard, focusing on being cited by AI through structured content and E-E-A-T. The 2026 checklist emphasizes proprietary data, multi-platform optimization, and human-centric content.

items.title: SEO vs AEO vs GEO: The Evolution Explained by Veteran Marketer
items.summary: SEO expert Josh Nay breaks down the differences: SEO for traditional rankings, AEO for direct answers in chatbots, and GEO for visibility in AI-generated summaries like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews. Smart brands now optimize for all three in parallel. It's time to level up beyond 2015 tactics.

items.title: Tools for GEO: Track Brand in ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini
items.summary: SEO consultant Faiz Israili highlights tools like Surfer, Semrush AI, and SE Ranking for monitoring brand appearances in AI answers. This practice is known as Generative Engine Optimization (GEO). Essential for modern content marketing strategies.

items.title: What's Hot, What's Not: AI Search Changes In Q1 2026 Recap
items.summary: A recap of Q1 2026 AI search developments highlights key changes in tools like Google AI Overviews and competitors. Trends show shifts in AEO/GEO practices and evolving algorithms. Marketers must stay updated on these rapid AI search evolutions.

items.title: Search Referral Traffic Down 60% For Small Publishers, Data Shows
items.summary: New data indicates a 60% drop in search referral traffic for small publishers, likely due to AI summaries reducing clicks. This trend underscores the shift towards zero-click searches and the need for GEO strategies. Content creators face challenges in driving direct traffic amid AI dominance.

items.title: Writers Publish Protest Book to Challenge AI Use of Copyrighted Works
items.summary: Writers have united to publish a protest book aimed at contesting AI companies' use of copyrighted works for training data. This symbolic publishing effort underscores the escalating copyright controversies surrounding AI in the literary world. The initiative seeks to draw attention to unauthorized use of authors' materials.

items.title: When AI Templates Went Too Far: The Romance Writing Scandal That Shook Publishing
items.summary: A scandal erupted in romance writing when AI templates were used extensively, leading to questions over authenticity and earnings. Affected authors had earned $890,000 in 2025 from novels that vanished amid revelations. The incident highlights risks of AI in genre publishing.

items.title: The BookTok Books Brady Lockerby Actually Recommends
items.summary: BookTok influencer Brady Lockerby, followed by over 700,000 people, shares her genuine must-read recommendations from viral titles. Amid widespread hype, she curates books worth the attention. The list features standout picks from recent BookTok trends.

items.title: Amazon Can Pay $3,000/Month Starting AI Publishing
items.summary: Paul Sims promotes AI publishing on Amazon as a lucrative alternative to TikTok or YouTube, potentially earning $3,000 monthly. He offers a free course detailing the process upon engagement. The method leverages AI for quick book creation and sales.

items.title: Don't Miss AI Publishing in 2026 Like Past Trends
items.summary: Tommi Pedruzzi shares how AI-generated 90-page nonfiction eBooks on Amazon KDP generate $3,000-$5,000 monthly. He provides a free 5-hour tutorial on the step-by-step process. The post urges action similar to early adopters of previous platforms.

items.title: Literary Snobbery Against BookTok and Popular Reads
items.summary: Dr David Vernon laments snobbery dismissing BookTok and readers' preferences. He encourages reading enjoyable works like Woolf, Wodehouse, or le Carré. Stresses that reading should bring happiness, not competition.

items.title: Oscars 2026: Has Hollywood’s “wokeism” run its course?
items.summary: Hollywood's persistent moral grandstanding and virtue signaling at award shows like the Oscars has led to audience fatigue and declining viewership from 23.6 million in 2020 to 18.1 million in 2025. Fans on social media decry preachy celebrities as hypocritical narcissists, preferring escapist entertainment over activism. The article questions if this trend signals the end of 'wokeism' in entertainment.

items.title: Rachel Zegler Addresses Snow White Casting Backlash
items.summary: Rachel Zegler described the backlash to her casting as Snow White over her Colombian heritage as confusing, noting she was criticized for not being enough of one ethnicity for West Side Story and too much for Snow White. She proudly embraces her roots and refuses to assimilate for others' comfort amid threats to her safety. The comments come after the Disney remake's significant box office flop.

items.title: Oscars 2026: 'One Battle After Another' Wins Best Picture as 'Sinners' Dominates
items.summary: At the 98th Academy Awards on March 15, 'One Battle After Another' claimed Best Picture along with awards for director and adapted screenplay. 'Sinners' had a huge night with Michael B. Jordan winning Best Actor and historic wins including Best Cinematography for a woman of color. The ceremony featured political statements, K-pop performance, and cast reunions amid some speech cutoffs sparking fan anger.

items.title: Jessie Buckley Surprises Woke Hollywood with Heartfelt Motherhood Tribute at Oscars
items.summary: Irish actress Jessie Buckley defied Hollywood's perceived anti-family agenda during her Oscar acceptance by delivering a touching tribute to motherhood. The moment contrasted with typical industry narratives and was celebrated as a refreshing pushback. It quickly went viral, highlighting audience appreciation for traditional values.

items.title: Rachel Zegler Doubles Down After Snow White Remake Flops Hard
items.summary: Rachel Zegler continues to face heat for her comments, refusing to assimilate following the Snow White remake's major box office disappointment. The post notes ongoing criticism tied to production remarks and casting controversies. It reflects broader audience rejection of the film's approach.

items.title: Oscars 2026 Venue Left Littered with Trash, Sparking Hypocrisy Backlash
items.summary: Post-ceremony photos revealed the Dolby Theatre trashed after the Oscars, drawing sharp criticism of Hollywood elites' entitlement. Detractors pointed to hypocrisy given stars' frequent virtue signaling on environmental and social issues. The images fueled discussions on industry disconnect from everyday audiences.

items.title: Paperclip: Open-Source Platform to Run Entire Companies with AI Agents
items.summary: Paperclip is an open-source operating system that enables running a company with zero human employees by orchestrating AI agents in roles like CEO, CTO, engineers, marketers, and more. Users define goals, hire agents, set budgets with governance and org charts, and monitor via a dashboard with full audit logs and heartbeats. This new tool addresses chaos in multi-agent management, ideal for solopreneurs and small businesses seeking autonomous operations.

items.title: Saifa AI Launches Private Business AI Platform Tailored for SMEs
items.summary: Saifa AI has unveiled a private business intelligence platform for small and medium-sized enterprises, training AI solely on proprietary data such as documents, product catalogs, customer interactions, and procedures. It provides a unified workspace to consolidate communications, manage knowledge, and streamline customer service and internal workflows. This move offers SMEs customized, secure AI capabilities without external data sharing.

items.title: AI Readiness Report: SME Optimism Outpaces Adoption
items.summary: ECI Software Solutions' March 11 report shows over 70% of SME leaders optimistic about AI for data analysis, marketing, customer service, and inventory, but adoption is hindered by skills gaps, data readiness issues, and 40% seeing no results. Labor shortages in key sectors heighten urgency for AI integration. The findings highlight the need for targeted strategies to bridge optimism and real business impact.
